title: Week 0 Quiz: How the Web Works

options: The IP address for a hostname
questions.explanation: DNS maps names to addresses (A/AAAA records). It never serves page content.

questions.prompt: A request returns 404. What is the most accurate interpretation?
options: The server was reached but has nothing at that path
questions.explanation: A 404 is an HTTP response, so the server was reached and answered.

questions.prompt: The #fragment part of a URL is sent to the server in the HTTP request.
questions.explanation: Fragments are handled only by the browser.

questions.prompt: Which of these happen between receiving HTML and seeing pixels? Select all that apply.
options: DNS lookup for the page host again
questions.explanation: The host's DNS lookup happened earlier. DOM, CSSOM, layout and paint are the rendering pipeline.

questions.prompt: Your page works with Live Server but a script with type="module" fails when you double-click index.html. Why?
options: file:// has no HTTP server and the browser blocks module loading from origin null
questions.explanation: Modules are fetched with CORS rules. file:// pages have an opaque origin, so the load is blocked.

questions.prompt: Which is the best element for the main navigation links?
questions.explanation: <nav> is a landmark that assistive technology can jump to.

questions.prompt: A placeholder is an acceptable replacement for a <label>.
questions.explanation: Placeholders disappear and are not reliably announced. Every input needs a label.

questions.prompt: Which selector wins: #card .title (id + class) or .card .title (two classes)?
options: The id selector, because it has higher specificity
questions.explanation: Specificity is compared as (ids, classes, elements): (1,1,0) beats (0,2,0).

questions.prompt: What does this print? const a=[1,2]; const b=a; b.push(3); console.log(a.length)
questions.explanation: b and a reference the same array. const prevents reassignment, not mutation.

questions.prompt: You render 200 cards from an array. What is the best way to handle clicks on a 'Delete' button inside each card?
options: Attach a listener to every button
Use one delegated listener on the list and check event.target.closest('button')
questions.explanation: Event delegation uses bubbling: one listener handles all current and future cards.

questions.prompt: Which is safest for inserting user-typed text into the page?
questions.explanation: textContent treats text as text, never as HTML, preventing injection (XSS).

questions.prompt: fetch('/api') returns a 500 response. What happens to the returned promise?
options: It resolves; you must check response.ok
questions.explanation: fetch rejects only on network failure. HTTP errors resolve with ok === false.

questions.prompt: A good data widget has which states?
questions.explanation: A blank widget on failure is the bug the Week 0 acceptance criteria are designed to prevent.
Missing or corrupted data makes it return null or throw. Wrap in try/catch and fall back to a default.

questions.prompt: Which sequence saves and publishes a change?
options: git add . ; git commit -m msg ; git push
git push ; git add ; git commit
questions.explanation: Stage, commit locally, then push to the remote.
